channel.title: Nature Materials
channel.description: Nature Materials is a multidisciplinary journal aimed at bringing together cutting-edge research across the entire spectrum of materials science and technology. Nature Materials covers all applied and fundamental aspects of the synthesis/processing, structure/composition, properties and performance of materials. Nature Materials provides a forum for the development of a common identity among materials scientists while encouraging researchers to cross established subdisciplinary lines. To achieve this, Nature Materials takes an interdisciplinary, integrated and balanced approach to all areas of materials research while fostering the exchange of ideas between scientists involved in different communities.

item.title: [7] Twist-angle-controlled anomalous gating in bilayer graphene/BN heterostructures
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Dominique Mailly, Rebeca Ribeiro-Palau

Authors: Gaia Maffione, Liam S. Farrar, Maëlle Kapfer, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant experimental study on graphene heterostructures and moire-related effects.

Tags: #graphene #moire #heterostructure

Abstract: Nature Materials, Published online: 06 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02667-7 Rotational misalignment between the top and bottom boron nitride layers encapsulating graphene acts as a switch for anomalous gating effects, such as gate ineffectiveness and hysteresis. These effects are observed at room temperature within an angle range of 15–45° and are highly sensitive to small angular changes.

item.title: [7] Multimodal scanning-probe quantum sensing of quantum materials
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Christian L. Degen, Chunhui Rita Du

Authors: Senlei Li, Vincent Jacques, Patrick Maletinsky, Christian L. Degen, Chunhui Rita Du

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Useful review on scanning probe techniques for quantum materials research.

Tags: #scanningprobe #quantumsensing #methods

Abstract: Nature Materials, Published online: 06 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02648-w Solid-state spin defects are a powerful and versatile class of quantum sensor. This Review covers the development of scanning-probe nitrogen-vacancy sensing as a tool for investigating quantum materials with nanoscale resolution, surveys the recent development of spin defects in 1D and 2D host materials and identifies key directions for future research.

item.title: [7] Excitons in van der Waals magnetic materials
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Xiaodong Xu, Vinod M. Menon

Authors: Pratap Chandra Adak, Florian Dirnberger, Swagata Acharya, Akashdeep Kamra, Xiaodong Xu, Vinod M. Menon

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Review on magnetic van der Waals materials, relevant to topological magnetism interests.

Tags: #magnetism #2Dmaterials #excitons

Abstract: Nature Materials, Published online: 03 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02636-0 In this Review, the interplay of excitons, magnons and photons in two-dimensional magnetic semiconductors and how this enables control of light–matter interactions are discussed, and promising opportunities for magneto-optic optoelectronic and quantum applications are surveyed.
